'''Onyeka Okongwu'''<ref>[https://www.nba.com/gamenotes/hawks.pdf Atlanta Hawks (41-41) (2-3) vs. Boston Celtics (57-25) (3-2) Thursday, April 27th, 2023, State Farm Arena, 8:30 pm EDT, Postseason Game #6, Home Game #3 (official Hawks game notes)] Retrieved May 23, 2023.</ref> (born December 11, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]].

Okongwu was a four-year starter at [[Chino Hills High School]] in California, playing alongside the Ball brothers, [[Lonzo Ball|Lonzo]], [[LiAngelo Ball|LiAngelo]], and [[LaMelo Ball]] for his first two years. As a freshman, he helped his team win the state championship and achieve national success, while being named [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Freshman of the Year|MaxPreps co-National Freshman of the Year]]. In his junior and senior seasons, Okongwu led Chino Hills to two more state titles, earning back-to-back [[California Mr. Basketball]] honors. He was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. In his only college season, Okongwu played for USC and was named to the first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]].

== Early life ==
Highly influenced by his older brother, Nnamdi, Onyeka grew a passion for basketball. Onyeka initially started playing around the age of 8 for Edge Basketball, a club program.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA rookie Onyeka Okongwu trained in Alex Cabagnot's youth league |url=https://www.spin.ph/life/people/pinoy-coaches-nba-draft-pick-no-6-onyeka-okongwu-a2442-20201127 |access-date=2023-08-02 |website= Spin.ph |language=en}}</ref> At age 11, Onyeka began playing for another program, RC Rebels, until he attended [[Secondary school|high school]].

While attending high school, Okongwu played alongside [[Jaylen Hands]] on the Compton Magic.

===Recruiting===
Okongwu finished his freshman season with offers to play college basketball for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]].<ref name=offers>{{cite web|last=Sondheimer|first=Eric|title=Chino Hills freshman Onyeka Okongwu offered by UCLA, USC|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/varsity-times/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-chino-hills-freshman-onyeka-okongwu-offered-by-ucla-20160201-story.html|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=December 3, 2017|date=February 1, 2016}}</ref> On May 14, 2018, he committed to USC over UCLA and [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]]. He was drawn to the program because of its proximity and coaching staff. Okongwu left high school as a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] on [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] and as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] on [[247Sports]].<ref name="commit">{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=May 14, 2018 |title=Five-star recruit Onyeka Okongwu chooses USC over UCLA, ASU |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/23503916 |access-date=June 11, 2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Okongwu immediately established himself as [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]'s best player.<ref name="draft">{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |last2=Wojnarowski |first2=Adrian |author-link2=Adrian Wojnarowski |name-list-style=and |date=March 25, 2020 |title=USC freshman Onyeka Okongwu opts to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28953136 |access-date=April 28, 2020 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> In his collegiate debut on November 5, 2019, he recorded 20 points, 13 rebounds and a school-record eight blocks to lead the Trojans to a 77–48 victory over [[2019–20 Florida A&M Rattlers basketball team|Florida A&M]]. He became the first USC player to post a [[double (basketball)|double-double]] in his debut since [[Taj Gibson]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite news |title=Okongwu's double-double leads USC over Florida A&M 77–48 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170557 |access-date=November 19, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 6, 2019}}</ref> On November 19, he scored a career-high 33 points, including 17 free throws, in a 91–84 win over [[2019–20 Pepperdine Waves men's basketball team|Pepperdine]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Thuc Nhi |title=Onyeka Okongwu dominates as USC stays unbeaten in victory over Pepperdine |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2019-11-19/onyeka-okongwu-dominates-usc-stays-unbeaten-victory-pepperdine |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=November 19, 2019}}</ref> The performance helped him claim [[Pac-12 Conference]] player and freshman of the week honors on November 25.<ref>{{cite web |title=USC's Okongwu first to sweep Pac-12 Men's Basketball weekly awards |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2019/11/25/uscs-okongwu-first-sweep-pac-12-mens-basketball-weekly-awards 2019 |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |access-date=January 27, 2020 |date=November 25, 2019}}</ref> On December 1, Okongwu recorded 27 points on 12-of-14 shooting, 14 rebounds and three blocks in a 77–62 victory over [[2019–20 Harvard Crimson men's basketball team|Harvard]] at the [[Orlando Invitational]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Onyeka Okongwu's 27 Points Lead USC Men's Basketball's 77-62 Rout ==Professional career==

===Atlanta Hawks (2020–present)===
Okongwu was selected with the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft by the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Quinn |first=Sam |title=2020 NBA Draft: Hawks select Onyeka Okongwu with No. 6 overall pick |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2020-nba-draft-hawks-select-onyeka-okongwu-with-no-6-overall-pick/ |access-date=November 18, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=November 18, 2020}}</ref> On November 24, 2020, the Hawks announced that they had signed Okongwu.<ref>{{cite web |last=Finberg |first=Annie |date=November 24, 2020 |title=Hawks Sign Onyeka Okongwu, Skylar Mays and Nathan Knight |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-onyeka-okongwu-skylar-mays-and-nathan-knight |access-date=November 24, 2020 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On July 21, 2021, the Atlanta Hawks announced that Okongwu had undergone surgery to repair a torn [[glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his right shoulder and Okongwu would be expected to be sidelined for about six months.<ref>{{cite web |last=Finberg |first=Annie |date=July 21, 2021 |title=Hawks Injury Update: Onyeka Okognwu |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-injury-update-onyeka-okognwu |access-date=July 21, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On January 13, 2023, Okongwu put up a career-high 20 rebounds alongside 18 points in a 113–111 win over the [[2022–23 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=January 13, 2023 |title=Collins beats buzzer with tip-in, Hawks edge Pacers 113-111 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401468788 |access-date=January 13, 2023 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On October 23, 2023, Okongwu signed a four-year, $62 million extension with the Hawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Caudell |first=Jackson |date=October 24, 2023 |title=NBA Analyst on Onyeka Okongwu's Extension With the Hawks: "That is a lock to age really, really well" |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/nba-analyst-on-onyeka-okongwus-extension-with-the-hawks-that-is-a-lock-to-age-really-really-well |access-date=October 24, 2023 |publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

On January 14, 2025, Okongwu put up 22 points and 21 rebounds in a 122–117 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He became the first player to record at least 20 points and 20 rebounds in a game off the bench in Hawks franchise history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hawks-news-onyeka-okongwu-accomplishes-feat-atlanta-player-history|title=Onyeka Okongwu accomplishes feat no other Hawks' player has done in history|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=January 14, 2025|access-date=January 14, 2025}}</ref> On January 21, Okongwu was moved into the starting lineup in place of [[Clint Capela]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hawk Adjust Starting Lineup: Onyeka Okongwu Takes Lead Role|url=https://bvmsports.com/2025/01/21/hawks-adjust-starting-lineup-onyeka-okongwu-takes-lead-role/|access-date=January 22, 2025|website=bvmsports.com|language=en|archive-date=January 22, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122083218/https://bvmsports.com/2025/01/21/hawks-adjust-starting-lineup-onyeka-okongwu-takes-lead-role/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 13, 2025, Okongwu recorded 32 points, 11 rebounds, 2 steals and 3 blocks, including 8 three pointers in the Atlanta Hawks’ 132–122 win over the [[Utah Jazz]]. The performance marked a career high in points and made three pointers. Okongwu became the third player in NBA history to record at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, 2 steals, 2 blocks, and 8 three pointers in a single game, joining [[LeBron James]] and [[James Harden]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jalen Johnson & Onyeka Okongwu’s Historic Games Power Hawks Win Over Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/jalen-johnson-onyeka-okongwus-historic-games-power-hawks-win-over-jazz |website=NBA.com |date=November 13, 2025 |access-date=November 13, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Onyeka Okongwu was born to Nigerian immigrants, Mike, and Kate Okongwu in [[Los Angeles]] on 11 December 2000. Onyeka and his siblings were raised in [[Chino, California|Chino]] by two hardworking parents. His mother works as a [[registered nurse]].<ref name="nguyen">{{cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Thuc Nhi |title=USC's Onyeka Okongwu stays grounded even as he rises on court |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2019-12-31/uscs-onyeka-okongwu-stays-grounded-even-as-he-rises-on-court |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=March 23, 2020 |date=December 31, 2019}}</ref> Highly influenced by his older brother, Nnamdi, Onyeka's passion for basketball began to grow. Okongwu's older brother, Nnamdi, also played basketball for [[Chino Hills High School]].<ref name="death">{{cite web|last=Gardner|first=Michelle|title=Chino Hills basketball player Nnamdi Okongwu, taken off life support, dies after skateboard accident|url=http://www.dailybulletin.com/2014/07/18/chino-hills-basketball-player-nnamdi-okongwu-taken-off-life-support-dies-after-skateboard-accident/|website=[[Inland Valley Daily Bulletin]]|access-date=December 3, 2017|date=July 18, 2014}}</ref> In 2014, Nnamdi sustained a [[brain injury]] in a [[skateboarding]] accident and later died after spending three days on [[life support]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Klemack|first1=John Cádiz|last2=Khan|first2=Samia|title=Freak Accident Leaves High School Basketball Star Brain Dead|url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/Accident-Leaves-Chino-Hills-High-School-Basketball-Star-Nnamdi-Okongwu-Brain-Dead-267468861.html|website=[[KNBC]]|access-date=December 3, 2017|date=July 17, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Rodriguez|first=Monica|title=Chino family grieves at loss of eldest son killed in skateboard accident|url=http://www.dailybulletin.com/2014/07/20/chino-family-grieves-at-loss-of-eldest-son-killed-in-skateboard-accident/|website=[[Inland Valley Daily Bulletin]]|access-date=December 3, 2017|date=July 20, 2014}}</ref> Okongwu wore the number 21 in honor of his brother, who had worn the same number while playing basketball.<ref name=db/> In January 2020, Chino Hills High School retired the number in honor of his late brother.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=Josh |date=2020-01-29 |title=Chino Hills Huskies boys' basketball to retire No. 21 for Nnamdi and Onyeka Okongwu |url=https://www.championnewspapers.com/sports_and_recreation/article_5a8e68ea-42f4-11ea-90ce-5bcac2968b74.html |access-date=2023-08-02 |website=Champion Newspapers |language=en}}</ref> Upon his arrival in [[Atlanta Hawks|Atlanta]], he switched numbers due to the team retiring the number 21 in honor of [[Dominique Wilkins]]. Again honoring his late brother, Okongwu began wearing the number 17 - the age Nnamdi was when he passed.<ref>{{cite web |last=Thompson |first=Jaylon |title=Onyeka Okongwu will wear No. 17 to honor late brother |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Onyeka-Okongwu-reveals-NBA-number-to-honor-late-brother-Atlanta-Hawks-USC-Trojans--155079169/ |website=247Sports |access-date=November 21, 2020 |date=November 21, 2020}}</ref> He also has a younger brother, Chukwuemeka (Also attended [[Chino Hills High School]]), and a younger sister, Chinemya.<ref name="pe">{{cite web|last=Wall|first=Stephen|title=Family recalls son as gentle giant|url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/2014/07/20/chino-family-recalls-son-as-gentle-giant/|website=[[The Press-Enterprise]]|access-date=December 3, 2017|date=July 20, 2014|archive-date=December 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171207090141/http://www.pe.com/2014/07/20/chino-family-recalls-son-as-gentle-giant/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Okongwu's father died in 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Spencer|first=Sarah K.|title=Nate McMillan gives update on Onyeka Okongwu|language=English|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/atlanta-hawks/mcmillan-gives-update-on-okongwu/FSBPVLQ7YZCKZJJBP2WQ4TNYJI/|access-date=2022-01-20|issn=1539-7459}}</ref>
